mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to expectations of tighter policy and reduced risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > prev(FEDFUNDS) + 0.25 in the following month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month period, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS crosses the trigger (Granger causality test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS for at least three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as investors anticipate easier financing and increased corporate investment.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < prev(FEDFUNDS) for three consecutive months
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are not statistically superior to the prior 60-day window mean (p > 0.05) during the three-month FEDFUNDS decline period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PAYEMS (labor market additions) accompanied by a simultaneous drop in UNRATE (unemployment) signals a tight labor market, which is associated with higher corporate earnings expectations and positive S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > prev(PAYEMS) * 1.15 AND UNRATE < prev(UNRATE) - 0.5 in the same month
failure_condition: During the trigger window, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly above the prior 20-day average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO (industrial production) falls by more than 2% in two consecutive months, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to weakening economic momentum and reduced equity risk premium.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < prev(INDPRO) * 0.98 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns remain positive or flat during the two-month INDPRO decline (median p-value > 0.5 in a bootstrap test).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in HOUST (housing starts) of at least 10% predicts a positive S&P 60-day forward return as it reflects resilient construction activity and consumer confidence, supporting equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > prev(HOUST) * 1.10 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the prior 60-day window mean during the three-month HOUST surge (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL (CPI) rises by more than 0.5% in a single month, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to immediate inflation concerns and preemptive rate hike anticipation.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > prev(CPIAUCSL) * 1.005 in a single month
failure_condition: Over a 6-month window, the 20-day forward returns during inflation spikes are not statistically lower than during baseline periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in PAYEMS and RSAFS (retail sales) of at least 5% in the same quarter indicate softening labor demand and consumer spending, which are associated with negative S&P 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < prev(PAYEMS) * 0.95 AND RSAFS < prev(RSAFS) * 0.95 in the same quarter
regime_hint: Labor demand and retail softness regime
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns remain positive or flat during the quarter of dual softening labor and retail indicators (median p-value > 0.5 in a rolling window test).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in GDPC1 (GDP) of at least 3% over four consecutive quarters is associated with a regime shift toward negative S&P 20-day forward returns as market anticipates economic contraction and lower growth equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < prev(GDPC1) * 0.97 for four consecutive quarters
failure_condition: During the four-quarter GDP decline, the 20-day forward returns are not persistently negative (less than 40% of windows negative in a 12-month window).
